BiblicalUsage: This is the Aramaic word for grass, and it stands in Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the great tree cut down. The stump is left bound in the tender grass of the field, and the king himself is told he will eat grass like an ox until he knows the Most High rules.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that grass in Daniel is the measure of a humbled king; the man who boasted over Babylon is brought down to the field, and the tender grass he once despised becomes his teacher.
